WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE Join the team designing AMD’s Zen high-performance processors. In this role, you’ll contribute to high-speed logic design and physical implementation of a microprocessor core, collaborating with engineers across the design flow to meet timing, power, and reliability goals. THE PERSON You enjoy solving complex logic design problems and are curious about what goes into a high-end microprocessor. You communicate clearly, collaborate well across disciplines, and are comfortable learning new tools and methodologies as you grow in the role. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Perform logic design and optimization. Execute custom place-and-route and physical implementation. Run synthesis and support implementation flows. Drive timing optimization and design closure using EDA tool flows (including static timing analysis). Analyze and address power, electrical, and reliability considerations (e.g., IR drop, electromigration, coupling/noise) as needed. Collaborate with cross-functional partners to bring designs from concept through silicon. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Digital logic design and optimization. Gate-level design experience. Timing analysis and optimization. Electrical reliability analysis. Knowledge of computer architecture. Experience with scripting languages (e.g., Perl, Python). Experience with industry CAD tools related to timing analysis, circuit analysis, and place-and-route. Familiarity with circuit and signal integrity topics (e.g., signal coupling/noise, IR drop, electromigration). ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer engineering or electrical engineering, or equivalent practical experience. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-DP1 #LI-HYBRID Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. AMD does not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services. AMD and its subsidiaries are equal opportunity, inclusive employers and will consider all applicants without regard to age, ancestry, color, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, race, religion, political and/or third-party affiliation, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates and will accommodate applicants’ needs under the respective laws throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. AMD may use Artificial Intelligence to help screen, assess or select applicants for this position. AMD’s “Responsible AI Policy” is available here. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

THE ROLE As a key member of AMD’s FPGA Product development team, you will design and implement cutting-edge IP features that power efficient, error-free, and on-time silicon delivery. You will leverage modern RTL design methodologies, advanced EDA tools, and AI-driven automation to accelerate integration and ensure first-time-right solutions. THE PERSON You are passionate about HW architecture, Digital design, and building cutting-edge silicon. As a strong problem solver and analytical thinker, you bring collaboration, communication, and adaptability to cross-functional teams spanning multiple time zones. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Collaborate with architects, hardware engineers, and SW-FW engineers to understand the product requirements and IP features. Build early-stage RTL designs based on product and architecture intent driving Silicon and Solution co-development. Build and enhance AI-driven infrastructure to accelerate IP integration and improve development timelines. Apply data-driven methodologies to align engineering teams across next-generation products and technology nodes. Support functional simulation and software quality checks, ensuring robust verification coverage. Partner with global teams to achieve seamless integration and delivery. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Expertise in RTL design (Verilog/SystemVerilog), including digital/analog block implementation. Understanding of VLSI design flow, from RTL through Physical Design and GDSII. Familiarity with Physical Implementation processes: floorplanning, synthesis, P&R, STA. Experience with EDA tools (Synopsys Design Compiler, Primetime, VCS; Cadence Virtuoso). Knowledge of UVM/OVM verification, simulation environments, and debugging. Understanding of FPGA architecture and usage models is a plus. Proficiency in scripting (Perl, Tcl, Python, Shell) for design automation. Excellent communication skills and ability to thrive in a fast-paced, global environment. ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering. THE ROLE: AMD’s Data Center GPU organization is transforming how AI and high‑performance computing are delivered at scale, and this role sits at the center of that effort. As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will act as a key execution leader and the customer’s voice within AMD’s Instinct™ GPU ecosystem, working closely with hardware, software, manufacturing, and business teams to bring complex programs from concept through successful customer deployment. You will help translate customer requirements into clear execution plans, anticipate and mitigate risks across hardware and software dependencies, and ensure AMD delivers industry‑leading AI and HPC platforms on time and at scale—all while collaborating with some of the brightest minds shaping next‑generation data center technology. THE PERSON: Successful candidates are strong program leaders who thrive in fast‑paced, technically complex environments. You bring structure to ambiguity, communicate clearly across diverse stakeholders, and take pride in driving execution from start to finish. You are comfortable operating at a systems level—understanding how hardware, software, and operational considerations come together—without needing to be the deepest technical specialist in the room. You build trust through accountability, influence without authority, and a proactive approach to identifying and resolving risks. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Collect, analyze, and translate customer feature requirements into actionable inputs for internal product development teams. Ensure customer‑required collateral is developed and delivered on time to support customer product development schedules. Coordinate with manufacturing and business operations teams to ensure sufficient part availability for initial deployments and field replacements. Track firmware, ROCm, and BKC versions to ensure correct hardware and software configurations in customer deployments. Develop and maintain integrated program schedules that account for driver, software stack, and hardware/firmware dependencies. Track product issues and accelerate resolution by supporting returns, coordinating failure analysis, and driving L1/L2/L3 debug escalation. Drive resolution of customer issues attributable to AMD manufacturing or assembly. Communicate program status, risks, issues, and mitigation plans to cross‑functional teams and leadership, and remove execution roadblocks. Proactively identify program risks, define prevention strategies, and implement corrective actions to reduce cost and schedule impact. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience leading complex technical or hardware‑adjacent programs in a data center, systems, or platform environment Exposure to server platforms, accelerated computing, or AI/HPC infrastructure Ability to operate across hardware and software organizations and manage interdependencies Experience working with geographically distributed teams and global stakeholders Familiarity with customer‑facing roles involving large‑scale or mission‑critical deployments Excellent interpersonal skills including the ability to work well with multiple people and teams, ability to communicate progress to team members on a regular basis Demonstrated experience leading programs across geographically distributed teams, including Asia and North America. Flexibility to support global program execution across time zones. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field LOCATIONS: Austin (preferred), San Jose, Seattle, Remote can be considered for the right candidate This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-DR2 #LI-Hybrid Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. THE ROLE: AMD is looking for a senior software engineer to join our growing team to help scale our test automation efforts. You will focus on automating test cases and building reliable test harnesses that accelerate firmware and platform validation across pre-silicon simulation models and post-silicon platforms. This role emphasizes creative automation: finding new ways to reduce manual effort, improve test coverage, and accelerate delivery using modern tooling — including AI assisted techniques and automation frameworks. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate possesses an innovative and problem-solving mindset, has a keen eye for Software engineering development, and is diligent and passionate about Technology. You are an inventive, results-oriented engineer who enjoys automating repetitive work and improving test reliability. You challenge the status quo, propose better ways to test and deliver, and enjoy applying new techniques (including AI/ML tools) to boost productivity. You communicate clearly with engineers across firmware, hardware and software domains, take ownership of test artifacts, and move quickly from prototype automation to production quality CI integration. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: With a primary focus on automation, create, execute and maintain detailed test procedures and test scripts for BIOS/IFWI and platform firmware using Python and other scripting tools. Scope, design and implement automation that runs across simulation environments and hardware platforms. Integrate test cases into Jenkins (or equivalent CI) pipelines and maintain CI jobs, reporting, and artifact collection. Use and extend internal hardware test tools and third-party utilities; capture failures, collect artifacts (logs, register dumps, AHDS captures), and report defects to firmware and system teams. Apply innovative automation approaches (including AI assisted test generation, test triage heuristics, or automated log parsing) to reduce manual effort and increase throughput. Collaborate with firmware developers, validation engineers, and simulation/modeling teams to reproduce issues in simulation (e.g., Simics like environments) and hardware. Help maintain and grow test frameworks, libraries and reusable test assets, so new tests are easy to author and run. Troubleshoot and debug test failures; contribute clear triage artifacts and constantly improve logging and debugging capabilities in our currently automated tests. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: . 3 or more years of professional experience in test automation, software development, or firmware validation Expert knowledge and hands-on experience in C, C++, Python Solid understanding of object-oriented-design principles Solid understanding of Software Engineering principles, Data structure, algorithms, Operating Systems concepts and multithread programming Excellent design and code development skills, familiarity with Linux and modern software tools and techniques for development Good analytical and problem-solving skills Experience with CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins or similar) and test job lifecycle. Practical debugging skills: collecting logs, interpreting kernel/firmware messages, and producing useful triage artifacts. Comfortable experimenting with automation-boosting tools and techniques (e.g., AI-assisted test generation, log parsing/analysis, or automation orchestration). Good knowledge of computer architecture and platform components (x86 processors/APU/GPU, PCIe, CXL, USB, NVMe) is advantageous. Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline LOCATION: Austin, Texas #LI-CS1 #LI-Hyrbid This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. THE ROLE: The Technical Fellow for High-Speed Interconnect and Optics is a senior technical leader responsible for defining and advancing NTSG’s system-level interconnect architecture for next-generation AI, HPC, and data center platforms. This role drives innovation across electrical and optical interconnect technologies—spanning ASICs, advanced packaging, boards, optics, and full-system integration—while shaping industry direction and contributing to AMD’s long-term technology roadmap THE PERSON: Defining next-generation interconnect architecture in this Lead role and long-term strategy for next-generation electrical and optical interconnects, including pluggable optics, co-packaged optics (CPO), co-packaged copper (CPC), and onboard optics (OBO), enabling scalable AI scale-up and scale-out system architectures. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Drive System-Level SI/PI Excellence Provide technical authority and leadership in high-speed signal integrity (SI) and power delivery network (PDN) design across ASICs, packages, boards, connectors, and optical interfaces. Ensure robust, end-to-end performance at 112G, 224G, and beyond under real-world system operating conditions. Lead Optical System Integration and Packaging Innovation Drive end-to-end optical system integration, including optics module architecture, silicon photonics, laser integration (internal and external), advanced packaging solutions, and thermal and power optimization for high-density systems. Guide SerDes and ASIC Co-Optimization Influence SerDes architecture, specifications, modeling assumptions, and tuning strategies to ensure alignment between ASIC design and real-world channel behavior, optical characteristics, packaging constraints, and system-level requirements. Hands-On Technical Leadership and Debug Serve as a hands-on technical authority during lab bring-up, characterization, and system debug. Resolve complex, cross-layer issues spanning SI/PI, optics, firmware, packaging, and system-level interactions across development and deployment phases. Shape Industry Direction and Ecosystem Alignment Represent AMD as a technical leader in industry standards bodies and consortia (e.g., OIF, IEEE, PCI-SIG). Influence next-generation specifications, drive ecosystem alignment, and ensure AMD’s interconnect roadmap leads and aligns with industry trends. Mentor and Multiply Technical Impact Mentor senior engineers, architects, and emerging technical leaders. Establish best practices, architectural frameworks, and design guidelines to elevate technical excellence across teams and business units. Influence Business and Product Strategy Act as a trusted technical advisor to senior leadership. Drive critical technical trade-offs, vendor and partner strategy, and product go/no-go decisions that materially impact product direction, risk, cost, and time-to-market. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Deep expertise in high-speed signal integrity and power integrity (SI/PI, PDN) for advanced data rates (112G, 224G, and beyond). Strong experience across optical interconnect technologies, including: Pluggable optics (QSFP, OSFP) Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Co-Packaged Copper (CPC) On-Board Optics (OBO) Proven experience in optical packaging and system integration, including silicon photonics, laser coupling strategies, and thermal and power management at scale. Hands-on experience with system bring-up, validation, and debug across ASICs, packages, boards, and optical subsystems. Strong understanding of SerDes architecture, equalization, FEC, and system-level channel modeling. Demonstrated ability to lead across organizational boundaries and influence vendors, partners, customers, and standards bodies. Track record of sustained technical leadership and architectural impact across multiple product generations. Recognized industry or academic thought leader; publications and patents a strong plus ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: PhD / Master’s in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Photonics, or a related technical field. Technical Manager, Server SoC Platform Emulation THE ROLE:  We are seeking a passionate, results‑driven, and innovative engineering leader to manage, lead, and develop an SoC Platform Emulation team. This team plays a critical role across both pre‑silicon and post‑silicon phases, working closely with Design, Firmware/Software, and Post‑Silicon Validation teams to shift left post‑silicon validation into the pre‑silicon emulation phase. The team is responsible for end‑to‑end HW+FW co‑verification, validating design and firmware together on platform‑level emulation environments. By identifying design, firmware, and system‑level issues early, the team enables higher‑quality silicon, faster post‑silicon bring‑up, and reduced post‑silicon validation cycles, ultimately accelerating time‑to‑market and improving product robustness. As a leader, you will drive cross‑functional collaboration, define execution strategy, build and mentor a high‑performing engineering team, and deliver scalable emulation workflows that support rapid silicon validation and long‑term platform success. THE PERSON:  The successful candidate is a passionate, technically strong, and execution‑focused engineering leader with the ability to operate effectively across organizational boundaries. They demonstrate: Strong system‑level thinking and technical judgment Proven people leadership, mentoring, and team‑building skills Ability to influence without authority and drive cross‑functional alignment Comfort operating in fast‑paced, milestone‑driven environments Clear communication skills with both technical teams and senior leadership KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead, manage, and develop an SoC Platform Emulation engineering team responsible for pre‑silicon and post‑silicon enablement across multiple SoC programs. Own and drive HW+FW co‑verification strategy on platform emulation environments to identify design, firmware, and system‑level issues early in the development cycle. Partner closely with Silicon Design, Firmware/Software, BIOS, and Post‑Silicon Validation teams to shift‑left post‑silicon validation into pre‑silicon emulation. Establish execution plans, priorities, and success metrics aligned with program milestones, tape‑out schedules, and validation readiness. Drive validation planning and execution for each SoC program to achieve program breakthroughs and readiness goals. Review execution status, validation coverage, risks, and mitigation plans across multiple programs, and drive issues to closure. Provide technical leadership and system‑level guidance, leveraging broad SoC and platform knowledge to resolve complex technical and cross‑functional issues, even where day‑to‑day ownership resides with IP technical leads. Lead and participate hands‑on in debugging complex system‑level problems, demonstrating strong problem‑solving skills and technical judgment. Drive continuous improvement in emulation infrastructure, workflows, coverage, and debug efficiency to improve product quality and reduce post‑silicon bring‑up time. In partnership with global validation leaders, identify, define, and implement improvements to post‑silicon validation methodologies to increase efficiency, predictability, and product quality. Develop and drive the strategic direction for validation automation, based on team needs and program requirements. Manage a team of approximately 10 engineers, including hiring, mentoring, performance management, and technical and career development. Communicate execution status, risks, and outcomes to cross‑functional partners and leadership in a clear, concise, and data‑driven manner. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience leading system‑level or platform‑level SoC emulation, or Pre Si verification/validation in a semiconductor environment. Strong understanding of SoC architecture, firmware/BIOS flows, and system software interactions. Hands‑on experience with pre‑silicon emulation platforms like Zebu, EP2, Palladium and understading of post‑silicon validation environments to shift left post si workloads to emulation Proven background in HW+FW co‑verification or integrated system validation. Experience working across global, multi‑site engineering teams. Demonstrated success driving shift‑left validation strategies or reducing post‑silicon bring‑up cycles. Experience building scripts, automations, or lightweight internal tools that improve creative workflows. Familiarity with AI/ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face) and model customization concepts. Strong understanding of creative production pipelines (design, motion, video, asset management). Ability to balance visionary creative direction with practical execution and operational rigor. THE ROLE: As a Functional Safety Manager at AMD, you will be directly impacting the certification of key AMD products, targeting critical AMD growth markets such as digital cockpit and autonomous driving. Your task will be to provide technical leadership for the product line safety function and for its customers. You will perform this in close cooperation with different functional owners within AMD. This challenging role will not only require extensive project leadership skills but also a thorough understanding of system safety standards within the automotive and industrial markets. THE PERSON: The successful candidate is a strong, collaborative leader who drives alignment across teams and partners to embed safety from the start. They bring a structured, practical approach to managing complex processes and ensuring high-quality, on-time delivery. A confident communicator, they effectively engage stakeholders and customers, including in audits and reviews. They operate with accountability and focus, balancing compliance with execution. Above all, they foster a positive, solutions-oriented culture that prioritizes safety and quality. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Functional Safety Strategy & Execution: Develop and drive AMD’s functional safety strategy aligned with ISO 26262, including defining safety plans and leading end-to-end execution across CPUs, GPUs, SoCs, and custom IP. Oversee core safety activities (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA, DFA), ensure ASIL compliance, implement safety mechanisms, and maintain full traceability from system requirements through validation. Cross-Functional & External Leadership: Partner across hardware, firmware, and software teams—as well as business units, suppliers, and customers—to embed safety into product roadmaps, align development efforts, and manage external interfaces (e.g., DIAs). Process, Compliance & Safety Case Ownership: Establish and continuously improve functional safety processes, lead audits and assessments, and own the development of safety cases and required work products to ensure compliance and production readiness. Organizational Enablement & Delivery: Build and mentor functional safety capabilities across teams, promote a safety-first culture, and take full accountability for delivering safety-compliant SoCs and systems, including direct engagement with customers during audits and reviews. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Functional Safety Expertise: Strong knowledge of ISO 26262, IEC 61508, and related standards, with proven experience in system-level safety analysis (FMEA, FTA, DFA) and development of ASIL-rated systems. Skilled in creating and managing safety work products, including safety plans and safety cases. Technical & Domain Knowledge: Solid understanding of semiconductor design flows (RTL, DFT, validation) and experience implementing safety architectures and mechanisms across SoCs, CPUs, GPUs, or similar high-performance platforms. Familiarity with automotive standards such as AEC-Q100 and ASPICE is a plus. Responsibilities:
THE ROLE AMD is seeking an experienced Performance Modeling Engineer to drive best‑in‑class system‑ and IP‑level performance for next‑generation AMD products, with a strong emphasis on I/O and memory‑subsystem performance. In this role, you will focus on pre‑silicon modeling through post‑silicon performance optimization, partnering closely with architects, designers, and verification teams to study performance behavior long before RTL is finalized. This is a highly visible, greenfield‑oriented role where your analysis and recommendations directly influence architectural tradeoffs, IP roadmaps, and real silicon outcomes in a fast‑moving, engineering‑driven environment. THE PERSON You bring a strong foundation in hardware architecture, performance analysis, and modeling, and you enjoy working at the intersection of data, architecture, and system‑level behavior. You are comfortable using cycle‑accurate and higher‑level models to study IP performance across realistic system workloads, identify bottlenecks, and propose practical architectural solutions. You are also a clear, effective communicator who can articulate complex performance findings, assumptions, and tradeoffs to cross‑functional partners and engineering leadership. You thrive in collaborative, low‑micromanagement environments and proactively share insights, progress, and recommendations that help teams make informed design decisions. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Study IP‑ and system‑level architectural performance using cycle‑accurate and abstract models across representative workloads. Participate in architecture exploration activities to evaluate performance tradeoffs across current and future AMD products. Identify performance bottlenecks in the IP pipeline and propose data‑driven architectural enhancements. Propose, execute, and oversee architectural case studies using existing silicon, RTL, and performance models. Expand, maintain, and document performance modeling frameworks and infrastructure. Support performance debugging and analysis in simulation, emulation, and post‑silicon environments. Investigate performance regressions, interpret results, and define follow‑up actions. Analyze trace captures from post‑silicon application workloads to inform optimization strategies. Analyze complex datasets to help define requirements and direction for next‑generation IP roadmaps. Interface closely with IP and SoC architects, performance verification leads, and performance working groups. Communicate findings clearly through meetings, presentations, written reports, and regular updates to engineering peers and management. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Hands‑on experience with system‑level or IP‑level performance modeling. Background in hardware architecture, RTL design, design verification, or related engineering roles. Strong object‑oriented programming skills using Python (preferred) and/or C++. Familiarity with PC and data‑center system architectures. Knowledge of I/O connectivity protocols such as PCI Express and CXL. Understanding of data‑center I/O workloads, memory bandwidth, and performance behavior. Working knowledge of I/O virtualization concepts, including MMU behavior, shared virtual memory, and x86 or ARM architectures. Exposure to accelerator‑based systems is a plus. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (preferred) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. LOCATION Austin, TX, This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-MO2

THE ROLE: We are seeking an experienced FPGA Power Management Engineer to join AMD’s FPGA Power Architecture team, helping bring adaptive, workload‑aware power management capabilities into next‑generation FPGA platforms. Drive timing closure for DVFS-enabled logic islands, including timing-constrained synthesis and place-and-route. Lead silicon bring-up and power characterization, using lab instrumentation to measure voltage droop, power-grid transients, and power profiles. Partner with silicon design, firmware, and validation teams to deliver scalable, production-ready power management solutions PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Demonstrated experience optimizing power consumption and performance using techniques such as DVFS and AVS. Practical experience with lab bring‑up, power integrity, telemetry, and power control interfaces (e.g., PMBus, SVI3). Familiarity with statistical power analysis techniques is a plus. Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across global teams. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Ph.D. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering preferred LOCATION: San Jose, CA, flexibility may be considered for exceptional candidates. Drive coordination across lab operations, infrastructure, and engineering teams to unblock rack access, power, networking, and test readiness. Partner with scale, performance, and automation teams to ensure workloads, stress tests, and regressions plans are ready before hardware arrives. Track high-impact failures (GPU, HSIO, FW, rack, network) through debug forums ensuring clear ownership and closure plans. Strong technical understanding of GPU-based AI systems, rack architectures, and datacenter infrastructure. Proven ability to manage ambiguity, drive debug execution, and lead cross-functional teams without direct authority. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level status reporting. Proficiency with program management and execution tools (Jira, Confluence, dashboards, Excel/PowerPoint). PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Hands-on experience with GPU cluster scale testing, system stress, or performance validation. Experience working through hardware/firmware debug cycles in pre-production or customer-facing environments. Develop and deploy ML/AI solutions for parametric outlier screening, drift detection, and excursion/anomaly detection across wafer, lot, site, and package dimensions. Perform in‑depth root‑cause analysis of yield loss and DPPM drivers by correlating test, fab, assembly, and design variables; distinguish systemic issues from statistical noise. Build, productionize, and maintain yield and quality analytics within AMD’s AVA analytics platform, moving models from experimentation to scalable deployment. Drive adaptive test, screening, and binning strategies using data‑driven insights to optimize product quality and manufacturing efficiency. Practical knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing and test flows, including wafer sort and final test, binning strategies, DPPM analysis, reliability screens, and excursion management. Demonstrated ability to deploy analytics or ML solutions into production environments, not just develop them in notebooks.
